implementation_notes: PactNet 5 is the .NET realization and carries the same structure as the other clients: Pact.V4(consumer, provider, config).WithHttpInteractions() returns an IPactBuilderV4 on which UponReceiving().Given().WithRequest().WillRespond() declare one interaction, and VerifyAsync(ctx => ...) starts the mock server, runs the client against ctx.MockServerUri and verifies the received requests. Provider verification uses the same package - PactVerifier(providerName, config).WithHttpEndpoint(uri).WithFileSource(pactFile).WithProviderStateUrl(...).Verify() - and because the Rust core calls the provider over TCP, the provider must listen on a real socket: hosting it in-process with TestServer/WebApplicationFactory makes every verification fail.
pitfalls: In-memory test hosting cannot be verified: the matching engine calls the provider over a real TCP socket, so TestServer/WebApplicationFactory must be replaced by a host bound to a URL.
PactNet ships the Rust core as a native library, so Linux musl and 32-bit targets are unsupported regardless of the managed target framework.
xUnit 2 does not capture console output, so verification output must be routed to ITestOutputHelper or the failure detail is lost.
